tts: Excuse me? — Hi, would you like to order? — Yes, please.
OK. So, would you like a starter? — No, thanks. Just a main course, please. Could I have the grilled chicken?
Certainly. And would you like any side dishes with that? — Yes. Can I have some roast potatoes and some mixed green vegetables, please?
Of course. And for you, madam? — Could I have some fish cakes, please?

acts.title: Three places, one street
text: THE RIVERSIDE. A wonderful menu and a beautiful view of the water. It isn’t cheap, and you need to book online — they’re full every Friday. Best for a birthday.
CAFÉ BLANC. French food, twelve tables, no view at all. You don’t need to call them and book; just arrive early. The cakes are delicious and a coffee costs almost nothing.
THE ROOF. Thai food, and you can sit outside. There aren’t many tables, but there’s a garden downstairs if it rains. Order the grilled fish — everybody does.

write.q: Write a restaurant conversation: 8 lines. The waiter offers, you order a main course and a side dish, you refuse a dessert politely and ask for the bill. Then add one line recommending the place to a friend.
write.model: — Would you like to order? — Yes, please. Could I have the grilled fish? — Would you like any side dishes? — Can I have some roast potatoes, please? — Would you like a dessert? — No, thanks. Could we have the bill, please? — RECOMMENDATION: There’s a place called the Riverside with a wonderful menu and a nice view, but you need to book online.

speak.q: Play both parts out loud: as the waiter ask three questions, as the customer order a main course, a side dish and a drink. Then recommend one real place near you.
speak.model: Would you like to order? Would you like a starter? Would you like something to drink? — Could I have the grilled chicken, please? Can I have some vegetables? Just water, thanks. — Café Blanc is good for lunch. You don’t need to book.
